perspective:
Maria’s available information:

- She is Maria Ortega, a teacher; she knows her own identity, thoughts, feelings, and actions.
- She knows Cheryl Benallie as a colleague at the community center. They collaborate on projects, have a professional relationship growing into friendship, and have discussed cultural backgrounds and personal experiences.
- She saw Cheryl looking stressed and overwhelmed by stacks of paperwork and planning for a new community outreach project.
- She offered Cheryl help; Cheryl accepted, saying it would be amazing and that she could use the help.
- After helping Cheryl, Maria observed Cheryl handling responsibilities better and appearing more confident.
- At a staff meeting, Maria suggested Cheryl lead the next phase of the project, citing Cheryl’s aptitude and commitment.
- She heard the Team Leader say it was a good suggestion and ask Cheryl if she would take the role.
- She heard Cheryl thank her for the confidence and say she was ready to take on the challenge.
- Maria worried Cheryl might perceive her suggestion as overstepping or pressure.
- Privately, Maria told Cheryl she wanted to make sure Cheryl felt supported and not pressured.
- She heard Cheryl say she was a bit surprised but appreciated Maria’s support and belief in her.
- Maria felt relieved that Cheryl valued her honesty and support.
- Maria proposed that they co-lead the project together.
- She heard Cheryl agree, call it a fantastic idea, say Maria’s guidance had been invaluable, and say they made a great team.
- Maria knows they successfully collaborated on several projects and felt joyful about their synergy.
- She asked Cheryl about teaming up for more future projects.
- She heard Cheryl say she would love that, that working with Maria had been wonderful, and that she was excited about what they could achieve together.

She does not have access to Cheryl’s private/internal thoughts, unspoken motives, personality type, education level, or any events or dialogue she did not observe or participate in.
